page: Microsoft Azure F48as_v6 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the Fasv6 family, powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. The system features 48 physical cores and 48 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz, with 1 thread per core. It is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor includes 32 KB of L1 instruction cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16) and cryptography standards like AES and VAES. No local storage is bundled with this instance, though it is Premium Storage capable, and it does not include any GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core scoring 147,728.85 and Geekbench multi-core reaching 23,839.0, both placing in the top 10% of tested servers. Single-core performance is also strong, with a stress-ng single-core score of 3,080.27 and a Geekbench single-core score of 2,101.0. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression performance is exceptionally high at 628.62 GB/sec, while single-threaded compression and decompression tasks fall into the average tier. Memory bandwidth is robust, delivering 230.45 GB/sec for large block read operations and 135.74 GB/sec for write operations. For specialized workloads, the server demonstrates top-tier efficiency in software compilation (64,173.0 on Clang) and image processing, alongside strong performance in ray tracing and text processing.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the F48as_v6 offers high compute density and strong multi-threaded performance per resource unit, making it suitable for compute-heavy workloads that do not require local NVMe storage. The primary tradeoff is the complete absence of local storage, requiring reliance on external Premium Storage, which may introduce latency or additional configuration overhead. Additionally, while the server excels at small to medium LLM inference—achieving 5,327.86 tokens/sec for 135M model prompt processing—its performance drops to average levels for large 70B models due to the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration. This server is best suited for multi-threaded applications, software compilation pipelines, image processing, database operations, and static web serving.
